title: Secrets, Credentials, and Safe Configuration
learningObjectives: Explain the core ideas and terminology of secrets, credentials, and safe configuration.
Recognize the risks or mistakes this topic is intended to prevent.
Apply appropriate defensive practices in a beginner project.
Distinguish this topic from related security concepts and controls.
Review a simple design and justify improvements using evidence.

understand.concept: Secrets include passwords, API keys, private tokens, and signing credentials. They should not be placed in source code, client bundles, logs, screenshots, or public repositories. Configuration separates environment-specific settings from program logic. Secret storage should use protected environment configuration or a dedicated secret manager, with access restricted and credentials rotated when exposure is suspected.
understand.whyItMatters: Leaked credentials can allow unauthorized access even when application code is otherwise well written.
understand.analogy: Think of a careful community space where entry, use of shared items, and privacy are guided by clear rules and appropriate checks.
understand.analogyLimit: Software security depends on technical boundaries, data flows, implementation details, and changing threats that this analogy cannot fully represent.

explain.narrative:
Secrets include passwords, API keys, private tokens, and signing credentials. They should not be placed in source code, client bundles, logs, screenshots, or public repositories. Configuration separates environment-specific settings from program logic. Secret storage should use protected environment configuration or a dedicated secret manager, with access restricted and credentials rotated when exposure is suspected.

Apply these principles proportionately. Use established platform and library protections instead of improvising security-critical mechanisms. For a real application, confirm requirements and review the implementation with qualified peers.

examples.code:

examples.explanation: A leaked credential must be revoked and replaced, not merely deleted from the latest file.

commonMistakes: Assuming a feature is safe because it works in normal use.
Trusting client-side controls as the only enforcement.
Applying one generic transformation to every kind of input or output.
Exposing credentials or personal data in source, logs, or screenshots.

independentTask.title: Independent Practice
independentTask.instructions: Create a configuration checklist for a small app with development and production settings. Include safe storage, access scope, logging restrictions, and a rotation plan without writing any real secrets.
requirements: Use a fictional or toy project and no real secrets or personal data.

hints: Assume anything shipped to the browser can be inspected.
Environment variables are not automatically secure if exposed to client builds or logs.
Remove secrets from logs and commits.
If exposed, revoke and rotate; history cleanup alone is not enough.

questions.explanation: Credentials can authorize access and must be protected.

questions.prompt: Where should server-side secrets generally be stored?
options: Protected server configuration or a secrets manager
questions.answer: Protected server configuration or a secrets manager
questions.explanation: Protected storage should control access to credentials.

options: Logs may be broadly accessible or retained and expose credentials
Logging is required to reveal passwords
questions.answer: Logs may be broadly accessible or retained and expose credentials
questions.explanation: Log access and retention can create exposure.

questions.prompt: What should happen after a credential is exposed?
options: Revoke it and rotate/replace it, then investigate
Only remove the latest code line
questions.answer: Revoke it and rotate/replace it, then investigate
questions.explanation: Deleting from current files does not invalidate a leaked credential.

options: Limit what a compromised credential can do
Make it easier to share publicly
questions.answer: Limit what a compromised credential can do
questions.explanation: Least privilege reduces the potential impact.
